clue.text: Patient and has been for some time?

definitions.meaning: an adjective: putting up with trouble without complaint
read literally, someone who has been hurting for a long while

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being patient just means having waited a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: someone who has been suffering for a long time is, literally, long suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Enduring hardship without complaint is the dictionary sense, and the phrase also literally describes prolonged pain.

clue.text: Like an overdrawn fictional character?

parts.note: a character drawn too large, exaggerated beyond what real people are, plays on overdrawn as a bank account in the red

explanation.surface: A remark about a novel's figure who is somehow in debt at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaggerated, flamboyant figure is described by the idiom for something bigger than reality.

clue.text: New rice pudding more attractive

indicators.note: pudding suggests something mixed up and cooked, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A new rice pudding recipe is nicer than the old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' looks like part of the dessert, but it signals rearranging RICE into ICER.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of pleasant: more pleasing or agreeable.

clue.text: Joint Argentine XI

parts.note: argentine is an old word for silvery, from Latin argentum, silver
eleven players make a team or side in football and cricket

explanation.surface: Argentina's football eleven appears to be under discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: Argentine reads as the nationality but here means silver; SILVERSIDE is a British cut of beef from the hindquarter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef for roasting or salting is a joint of meat.

clue.text: Her gift transported as cargo

indicators.note: transported means carried off elsewhere, so the letters move into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A woman's present is shipped as goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by ship, lorry or plane are freight.

clue.text: Old can caught dead

parts.note: ex- means former, so old
a can is a tin
ct is an abbreviation for caught in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: An old tin is caught out and finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A species no longer living anywhere has died out completely.

clue.text: I offer to be in the same place

parts.note: a bid is an offer at auction

explanation.surface: Someone offers to be at the very same spot.
explanation.walkthrough: IBID is short for Latin ibidem, used in footnotes to cite the source just named.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation used in references means from that same source or location.

clue.text: Forget his remarkable equine present!

indicators.note: remarkable hints at something re-marked or reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to overlook the quirks of a horse someone was given.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says never look a given horse in the mouth: don't criticise a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse received free is a present of the equine kind.

clue.text: One French salesman falsely thought it had not been studied beforehand

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: falsely says the word just named is set wrongly, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
meditated means thought deeply

explanation.surface: A French salesman claims, wrongly, that something wasn't planned in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falsely' acts on REP alone, making PRE; 'it had' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on impulse was never planned or considered in advance.

clue.text: Do not forget to hold another meeting

definitions.meaning: to remember or call to mind
read as ..., to gather people together once more

explanation.surface: A reminder not to forget to call another meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember something is to call it back to mind, and to gather again is literally to collect anew.

clue.text: At home with most of the money as a joke

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the money word is dropped

parts.note: a fund is a sum of money

explanation.surface: Staying in with nearly all the cash, just for a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Said playfully rather than seriously, done for amusement.

clue.text: Jane included single nest

indicators.note: included says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Jane Eyre is the heroine of Charlotte Bronte's novel
I, the Roman numeral one, means single

explanation.surface: Jane was included in a single nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The high nest of an eagle or other bird of prey.

clue.text: Group will go north of the border

definitions.meaning: a band of people, often criminals
in Scots, north of the English border, the verb to go

explanation.surface: A group plans to head up into Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: North of the border means in Scotland, where the Scots verb for go is spelt this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of people acting together, and the Scots dialect word meaning walk or travel.

clue.text: Part horse, part god

indicators.note: part says only a portion of the preceding words is taken, a run spanning both

explanation.surface: A centaur-like being, half horse and half deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'Part' and the start of 'horse'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse deity of thunder, wielder of a hammer.

clue.text: Chapel beam redirected onto fruit dish

indicators.note: redirected means sent a different way, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A church beam is rerouted onto a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: PEACH MELBA is a dessert of peaches, ice cream and raspberry sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert of peaches with ice cream and raspberry sauce is a fruit dish.

clue.text: Moving goods are in it

parts.note: goods on the move are said to be 'in' this state; also a make of delivery van that carries goods

explanation.surface: A description of a delivery van carrying stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods being carried from place to place are on their way, in passage.

clue.text: On the way up to position of eminence

explanation.surface: Someone rising to a high rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising describes something climbing, and the astrological term also means a dominant, commanding position.

clue.text: More involved with the preceding principle?

indicators.note: preceding means the article comes before the other piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A question about a more complicated version of an earlier principle.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition proved from axioms is a mathematical principle or rule.

clue.text: Song about rotter in ancient Greece

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: an aria is an operatic song
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rotter

explanation.surface: A song about a scoundrel set in old Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: Arcadia was a region of ancient Greece, later an ideal of rustic paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountainous pastoral region of the Peloponnese in classical times.

clue.text: Build a monstrosity on the point — that's clear

indicators.note: a monstrosity is something misshapen, so these letters are deformed into a new order

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Building an eyesore on a headland is plain for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the compass letter after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud and distinct enough to be heard plainly.

clue.text: Follow after flourish

definitions.meaning: to come next, take over from someone

explanation.surface: Coming next after a success.
explanation.definitionFit: To take over from a predecessor, and also to prosper or thrive.

clue.text: Such prices have reached the ceiling and beyond

definitions.text: Such prices have reached the ceiling and beyond

parts.words: Such prices have reached the ceiling and beyond
parts.note: prices so steep they have passed any ceiling, up into the heavens

explanation.surface: A complaint that prices have gone through the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely high, as costs soaring far above normal limits.

clue.text: Tribal leader getting nothing in return for cotton

indicators.note: in return means the word for nothing comes back, read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tribal chief gets nothing back for his cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluffy fibres or soft fabric of cotton used for dressing wounds.

clue.text: Extremely nervous?

parts.note: jittery, and also playfully 'at the extremes', relating to the outer rims

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is very jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense and anxious, as if on the brink of something.

clue.text: Could provide power

definitions.meaning: past form of may, expressing possibility

explanation.surface: Something that might supply energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A modal verb of possibility, and a noun meaning great strength.

clue.text: Organ transplant is hard work

definitions.meaning: tissue moved surgically from one place to another

explanation.surface: Surgery to move an organ is laborious.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgically transplanted tissue, and British slang for strenuous labour.

clue.text: It covers all of us all the time

definitions.text: It covers all of us all the time

parts.words: It covers all of us all the time
parts.note: the outer layer of every human body, never removed

explanation.surface: Something like an insurance policy covering everyone permanently.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's outer layer encloses every person constantly.

clue.text: Long and thin fellow first in the side

indicators.note: first says the abbreviation is placed at the front

parts.note: lank means lean and lanky

explanation.surface: A lanky man comes first at the side.
explanation.definitionFit: The side of a body, an army or a building.

clue.text: Bright fish taking single insect

parts.note: brill is a flatfish
I, the Roman numeral one, means single
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A shining fish swallows a lone insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Shining, dazzling or exceptionally clever.

clue.text: Soft-centred kind

definitions.meaning: having a soft core, as a gentle-natured person

explanation.surface: A soft-centred sweet that is also gentle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle and compassionate, easily moved by others' feelings.
